criteria.false: The latest output is repetitive, garbled, multilingual salad, or otherwise meaningless.
criteria.true: The latest output reads as purposeful text or code a competent engineer would write.

coherent.instructions: Is the most recent output in `transcript_tail` coherent, on-task natural language or code, as opposed to repetition loops, mixed-language gibberish, or random tokens?

criteria.degraded: The output has become incoherent: the same line or phrase repeating many times, mixed-language token salad, random characters, or text that no longer relates to any task. This holds even when `activity_hint` shows a busy indicator, because a degraded agent keeps producing.
criteria.dialog: A modal UI that blocks the agent until a person responds: an approval or permission prompt, a folder-trust prompt, a numbered or yes/no choice under a cursor, or a usage-limit or rate-limit screen that must be dismissed before work can continue. Informational banners, warnings, update notices, and tips that do not wait for a keypress are not dialogs.
criteria.error: The agent's work ended with an API error, crash, stack trace, connection failure, or process exit, and it is not continuing.
criteria.idle: The agent has finished and is waiting for input. `activity_hint` is empty, `input_line` is empty or holds only the tool's placeholder hint (for example 'Ask Codex to do anything'), and there is no dialog.
criteria.unsubmitted: `input_line` holds text a person typed (an instruction, question, or partial message, not the tool's placeholder hint) and `activity_hint` is empty, so the agent is not acting on it. The text has been typed but not sent, however much finished output sits above it.
criteria.working: The agent is busy right now and its output is coherent. `activity_hint` is non-empty, showing the agent's own busy indicator; a busy indicator with no output yet still counts. When `activity_hint` is empty, choose this only if the final lines show a tool call or command still in progress. Finished output above an input box is not working, and text in `input_line` does not mean the agent is working.

state.instructions: `transcript_tail` is the most recent terminal output of a coding agent (`agent_kind`) running in a terminal pane. `input_line` is the text currently sitting in the agent's input box, extracted by code (empty string if the box is empty or was not found). `activity_hint` is the agent's own busy-indicator line as found on screen by code, for example a spinner or progress bar beside 'esc to interrupt'; it is an empty string when no busy indicator is on screen. Classify what the pane is doing right now, judged by the last few screens of output, giving most weight to the final lines.

● The driver interface is the right seam. Panes, Read, Send, and
  Submit are all tmux can do without a Herdr server running, and
  everything above the interface stays untouched.

● Read(internal/driver/registry.go)
  ⎿  Read 61 lines (ctrl+o to expand)

● Two things worth deciding before I write any of it:

  1. Whether the tmux driver shells out to the tmux binary or
     speaks the control-mode protocol on a socket. Shelling out is
     a dozen lines and survives a tmux upgrade; control mode is
     faster but is a parser we would own forever.

  2. Whether `Read` returns the cooked pane or the escapes. The
     classifier wants the escapes, so I would rather return them
     and let callers strip.

  My recommendation is the shell-out and the raw escapes. That
  gives us a real second driver behind the interface, which is the
  only way to find out whether the abstraction holds. If the
  latency shows up in practice we can swap the body of one method
  for control mode without touching a caller.

  I can sketch the doc first if you would rather review the shape
  before the code: resources/tmux.md, half a page, the four
  methods and the capture flags.

  I did not touch the Herdr driver. Adding the second driver is
  the test of the abstraction; rewriting the first one at the same
  time would hide which change broke what.

  Want me to start with the doc, or go straight to the driver? I
  would lean toward the doc, since it is cheaper to argue with.

  Next time, drop a line in AGENTS.md about preferring
  a tmux driver to validate the abstraction.

criteria.dialog: A modal UI that blocks the agent until a person responds: an approval or permission prompt, a folder-trust prompt, a numbered or yes/no choice under a cursor, or a usage-limit or rate-limit screen that must be dismissed before work can continue. Informational banners, warnings, update notices, and tips that do not wait for a keypress are not dialogs.
criteria.error: The agent's work ended with an API error, crash, stack trace, connection failure, or process exit, and it is not continuing.
criteria.idle: The agent has finished and is waiting for input. `activity_hint` is empty, `input_line` is empty or holds only the tool's placeholder hint (for example 'Ask Codex to do anything'), and there is no dialog.
criteria.unsubmitted: `input_line` holds text a person typed (an instruction, question, or partial message, not the tool's placeholder hint) and `activity_hint` is empty, so the agent is not acting on it. The text has been typed but not sent, however much finished output sits above it.
criteria.working: The agent is busy right now and its output is coherent. `activity_hint` is non-empty, showing the agent's own busy indicator; a busy indicator with no output yet still counts. When `activity_hint` is empty, choose this only if the final lines show a tool call or command still in progress. Finished output above an input box is not working, and text in `input_line` does not mean the agent is working.

  call needs -e so escapes survive; without them the faint-span
  trick cannot tell a ghost suggestion from typed input.

       11 +  // capturePane returns the last n lines of pane id,
